papers.title: SwarmEvolve: Latent Agent Swarms for Evolutionary Discovery and Optimization
papers.abstract: LLM-guided evolutionary search uses AI agents to improve programs for mathematical and computational problems by iteratively refining solutions and combining high-scoring methods. However, the process is often slow because the LLM generates a long textual chain of thought for each round and must repeat this generation many times to maintain population diversity. We present SwarmEvolve, a framework in which hundreds of low-cost agents per round work in swarms, reason in latent space without decoding to text, and share information by passing KV caches. Each swarm studies the problem from a different angle. A novelty filter keeps the most distinct agent ideas by directly measuring the distances between the agents' hidden state vectors. Crossover of ideas happens naturally in latent space, as a summarizer agent receives the combined KV caches of all swarm members. On 21 problems in mathematical discovery and scientific computing, SwarmEvolve gets the highest average score and needs a median of only 3 to 8 minutes to reach the best scores that other state-of-the-art frameworks reach in 60 minutes. On several problems, SwarmEvolve with Qwen3 8B improves on the solutions that AlphaEvolve first found with frontier LLMs. Our work shows that agent swarms that communicate in latent space offer a fast, low-cost approach to program search for scientific problems.
papers.summary_zh: LLM引导的进化搜索通过迭代优化和组合高分方案来改进程序，但每轮生成长文本思维链且需多次重复以维持种群多样性，导致过程缓慢。SwarmEvolve让每轮数百个低成本智能体以群体方式在潜空间中推理而无需解码为文本，通过传递KV缓存共享信息，并用新颖性过滤器基于隐藏状态向量距离保留最独特的想法，在潜空间中自然完成想法交叉。在21个数学发现与科学计算问题上，SwarmEvolve取得最高平均分，达到其他最先进框架60分钟才能取得的最佳分数仅需中位数3至8分钟，并在部分问题上用Qwen3 8B超越了AlphaEvolve用前沿LLM首次找到的解。
papers.summary_en: LLM-guided evolutionary search improves programs for mathematical and computational problems by iteratively refining and combining high-scoring solutions, but it is slow because the LLM generates long textual chain-of-thought each round and must repeat this many times to maintain population diversity. SwarmEvolve lets hundreds of low-cost agents per round work in swarms, reason in latent space without decoding to text, and share information by passing KV caches, with a novelty filter keeping the most distinct ideas via hidden-state distances and crossover occurring naturally when a summarizer agent receives combined KV caches. On 21 problems in mathematical discovery and scientific computing, SwarmEvolve achieves the highest average score and needs a median of only 3 to 8 minutes to reach best scores that other state-of-the-art frameworks reach in 60 minutes, and with Qwen3 8B it improves on solutions AlphaEvolve first found with frontier LLMs on several problems.
highlights_zh: 潜空间群体推理与KV缓存通信
中位数3-8分钟达他人60分钟最佳分
低成本8B模型可超越前沿LLM解
highlights_en: Latent-space swarm reasoning with KV-cache communication
Median 3-8 min to match others' 60-min best scores

papers.title: Scientist World: Grow a Research World for AI-Scientists
papers.abstract: AI-Scientists arrived, but a world for them to grow in did not. Human scientists take theirs for granted $-$ centuries of open problems and shared ideas, waiting in the scientific literature. To AI-Scientists, that world is readable but not runnable, so we build Scientist World for them: every research paper becomes an executable environment. Our autonomous pipeline extracts each paper's open-ended research question and reproduces its proposed method as the baseline; an AI-Scientist entering the environment is evaluated against what the human authors achieved. We release the first 1,000 verified environments. With the world as an evaluation, we found that frontier AI-Scientists can already surpass the human researchers 74% of the time. As a record of how AI does science, it contains 6,400 hours of research traces, with every idea, experiment, failure, and success. As a training ground, we are able to raise (+158%) a small model to match frontier models in research ideation. At last, AI-Scientists' own world has arrived, grown from and growing with science itself.
papers.summary_zh: AI-Scientist已出现，但缺乏可供其运行和成长的研究环境，科学文献对其只可读不可执行。作者构建Scientist World，将每篇论文转化为可执行环境，自动提取开放研究问题并复现原方法作为基线，供AI-Scientist对照人类作者成果进行评估。首批发布1000个已验证环境，发现前沿AI-Scientist已有74%概率超越人类研究者，并积累6400小时研究轨迹，还能将小模型研究构思能力提升158%以媲美前沿模型。
papers.summary_en: AI-Scientists have arrived, but there is no runnable world for them to grow in, since the scientific literature is readable yet not executable for them. The authors build Scientist World, turning each paper into an executable environment that extracts its open-ended research question and reproduces its method as a baseline, so an entering AI-Scientist is evaluated against what the human authors achieved. They release the first 1,000 verified environments, find that frontier AI-Scientists already surpass human researchers 74% of the time, record 6,400 hours of research traces, and raise a small model by 158% to match frontier models in research ideation.
highlights_zh: 论文转为可执行研究环境
AI-Scientist 74%超越人类
小模型构思提升158%

papers.title: User Embeddings are Superpositions of Interpretable Behavioral Modes
papers.abstract: User embeddings are central components of modern recommendation, personalization, and behavioral modeling systems. Though these embeddings can compactly encode rich behavioral information, they are inherently dense and opaque, limiting interpretability. To address this gap, we argue that user embeddings can be understood as sparse superpositions of interpretable behavioral modes. This structure is directly predicted by generative models of user behavior for linear embeddings and extends approximately to deep-learning representations by the superposition hypothesis. Superimposed modes can naturally be recovered by sparse dictionary learning methods, such as sparse autoencoders (SAEs), and recovered modes can be automatically named and queried in natural language. We validate mode recovery against known ground truth on synthetic data, where SAEs recover modes better than classical sparse baselines, including on transformer-encoded embeddings. We then apply the method to classical and transformer-based user embeddings from two real-world datasets. We also show how the corresponding natural-language labels enable zero-shot audience retrieval and characterization over embeddings never trained on text. The framework is post-hoc and model-agnostic, requiring no modification to the upstream embedding system.
papers.summary_zh: 用户嵌入虽能紧凑编码丰富行为信息，但本质稠密且不透明，限制了可解释性。作者提出用户嵌入是可解释行为模式的稀疏叠加，并用稀疏自编码器等稀疏字典学习方法事后恢复这些模式，还能用自然语言自动命名和查询。在合成数据上SAE优于经典稀疏基线，在真实数据上实现了零样本受众检索与刻画，且方法模型无关、无需改动上游系统。
papers.summary_en: User embeddings compactly encode rich behavioral information but are dense and opaque, limiting interpretability. The authors argue that user embeddings are sparse superpositions of interpretable behavioral modes, recoverable via sparse dictionary learning such as sparse autoencoders (SAEs) and automatically nameable and queryable in natural language. On synthetic data SAEs outperform classical sparse baselines, and on two real-world datasets the method enables zero-shot audience retrieval and characterization in a post-hoc, model-agnostic way without modifying the upstream embedding system.
highlights_zh: 提出嵌入为可解释行为模式的稀疏叠加
SAE在合成数据上优于经典稀疏基线
支持零样本受众检索且模型无关

papers.title: Unpacking the Compute Efficiency of Strong-to-Weak OPD against GRPO
papers.abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) trains a student on its own rollouts under a frozen teacher's per-token supervision. Does this dense signal reduce the training FLOPs needed to reach a target accuracy compared with reinforcement learning? We systematically compare vanilla reverse-KL OPD with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) across task difficulty, student and teacher size, domain, and optimization choices, measuring held-out accuracy against training FLOPs. With an external post-trained teacher, OPD generally loses to GRPO in accuracy per training FLOP at matched settings, even when the teacher is further trained with GRPO, and often suffers response-length inflation. Yet a different teacher changes the picture: when the teacher is the student's own GRPO checkpoint, OPD recovers that checkpoint's accuracy on math with $50\times$ fewer distillation FLOPs than GRPO needs to reach the same accuracy. Following the same teacher setting, we consistently observe this high efficiency with a larger student, on code, and in a second model family. On a single domain, however, the GRPO checkpoint is already the desired model, so distilling it adds to total compute. Across domains, separate GRPO checkpoints hold different capabilities, and no single checkpoint serves every domain. Multi-teacher OPD (DeepSeek-AI, 2026) consolidates per-domain GRPO experts into a single student that matches each expert's accuracy, with the distillation stage costing only 5.2% (on 2 domains) and 8.0% (on 4 domains) of the specialist training FLOPs. Counting specialist training and distillation together, this pipeline reaches joint GRPO's performance on the 2-domain mix with 42.0% fewer total FLOPs.
papers.summary_zh: 论文比较在线策略蒸馏（OPD）与GRPO在达到目标准确率时所需训练FLOPs的效率，回答密集教师监督能否降低计算成本。作者系统扫描任务难度、师生规模、领域与优化选择，并区分外部后训练教师与学生自身GRPO检查点两类教师设置。结果显示外部教师下OPD通常不如GRPO且易致回答膨胀，但以学生自身GRPO检查点为教师时数学上仅需1/50蒸馏FLOPs即可复现精度，多教师OPD整合领域专家可在2领域混合上比联合GRPO少42%总FLOPs。
papers.summary_en: This paper asks whether on-policy distillation (OPD) with dense teacher supervision reduces training FLOPs to a target accuracy compared with GRPO. The authors systematically sweep task difficulty, student/teacher size, domain, and optimization choices, distinguishing external post-trained teachers from the student's own GRPO checkpoint as teacher. With external teachers OPD generally loses accuracy per training FLOP and inflates response length, but with the student's own GRPO checkpoint OPD recovers math accuracy with 50x fewer distillation FLOPs, and multi-teacher OPD consolidating per-domain experts reaches joint GRPO performance on a 2-domain mix with 42.0% fewer total FLOPs.
highlights_zh: 区分外部教师与自身GRPO检查点两类教师设置
自身检查点蒸馏数学达同精度仅需1/50 FLOPs
多教师整合2领域省42%总算力但单领域不划算

papers.title: Label-Wording Augmentation in a Typed-Decision Encoder: Gains on Unfamiliar Words, Not on Abbreviations or Codes
papers.abstract: Typed-decision models score options that the caller supplies at request time, so their accuracy depends on label wording that the model's developer does not control. We compare two releases of a 307M-parameter multilingual cross-encoder, Ru-Jev, trained on thirteen Russian-language tasks; the later release adds an augmentation that presents labels in several surface forms. Holding questions fixed and varying only how eighteen routing labels are worded, we evaluate ten label vocabularies, produced by three separate processes and checked for overlap with the training data, with five candidates per question and, for eight of them, also with eighteen. On held-out vocabularies made of ordinary or borrowed words (English-derived jargon, office slang, department names), the augmented release is more accurate in every setting, by up to 0.24. Eleven of these fourteen gains survive a Holm correction (slang with eighteen candidates and descriptive sentences with five do not), and for jargon on all labels the label-level interval excludes zero in both settings. On abbreviations and opaque codes it gives no usable gain: on abbreviations it is not better, and worse on the clean slice, and on opaque codes both releases stay at or below chance once labels related to training options are removed. In most cells where accuracy rises, the risk-coverage area falls, but with eighteen candidates confident errors rise on jargon and slang. On two datasets neither release saw, accuracy moves by -8.4 and +5.6 points. We also report four evaluation hazards from comparing the two releases.

papers.title: Do You Miss the Nights We Spent Crafting Figures? Rethinking Teaser and Framework Figures in the Age of Generative AI
papers.abstract: Scientific figures give research ideas a visual form through choices of abstraction, composition, and emphasis. Generative AI offers new ways to realize these choices, raising questions about explanatory clarity and purposeful visual expression. We examine these questions through a visual retrospective of 371 motivation and framework figures from 200 papers. The corpus comprises a quota-based main sample of 160 papers spanning four temporal periods and a separate purposive style-contrast sample of 40 papers. A single multimodal judge evaluates six dimensions of communication and design, with three repeated judgments per figure. We attempt source-constrained revisions of all 371 figures, of which 369 pass the recorded fidelity checks. Original-figure ratings show no uniform decline across periods. Revisions increase mean clarity ratings by 0.428 points and decrease aesthetic coherence ratings by 0.111 points on a five-point scale. Gains in the six-dimension average are larger for main-sample motivation figures than for frameworks. Case analyses show that added explanation can clarify comparisons while leaving typographic hierarchy and visual economy unresolved. These model-based findings support researcher-led design, with AI assisting exploration and authors retaining responsibility for explanatory purpose, composition, and scientific relationships. The accompanying atlas and evaluation records are available at https://ntu-ai4x.github.io/Rethinking_Figures/index_en.html.
papers.summary_zh: 生成式AI为科研配图提供新手段，但动机图与框架图在解释清晰度和视觉表达上的实际效果尚不明确。作者对200篇论文的371幅图做视觉回溯，用多模态评判器按六维度重复评分，并尝试源约束修订其中369幅。结果显示修订使清晰度均值升0.428分、审美连贯性降0.111分，动机图增益大于框架图，说明AI宜辅助探索而解释目的与构图仍应由研究者负责。
papers.summary_en: Generative AI offers new ways to realize abstraction, composition, and emphasis choices in scientific figures, but their explanatory clarity and purposeful visual expression remain unclear. The authors conduct a visual retrospective of 371 motivation and framework figures from 200 papers, rating six communication and design dimensions with a multimodal judge and attempting source-constrained revisions of 369 figures. Revisions raise mean clarity by 0.428 and lower aesthetic coherence by 0.111 on a five-point scale, with larger gains for motivation figures than frameworks, supporting researcher-led design with AI as an exploration aid.
highlights_zh: 371幅图六维度多模态重复评分
AI辅助探索，作者保留设计责任

papers.title: Where and Why is Grounded Reasoning Useful?
papers.abstract: Grounded reasoning, where a model outputs text coordinates of relevant locations in chain-of-thought reasoning, is a common strategy for solving complex visual reasoning problems. However, the benefits and limitations of grounded reasoning are understudied. We study where and why grounded reasoning is most useful. To do so, we introduce a chain-of-thought analysis method to measure how much a model uses its outputted grounding in its thinking trace and perform a detailed ablation study of a grounded reasoning training recipe. We find that grounded reasoning improves counting but shows no significant gain over baselines without coordinate grounding across a wide range of spatial reasoning and perception benchmarks. Using several synthetic tasks, we show that grounded reasoning is most useful when a task requires undescribable references, which are visual concepts that are difficult to describe in language. However, we observe that many existing visual reasoning benchmarks are solvable with only describable text references. To close this gap, we introduce BrickVision, a new benchmark that requires undescribable visual references to solve.
papers.summary_zh: grounded reasoning（在思维链中输出相关位置的文本坐标）被广泛用于复杂视觉推理，但其收益与局限缺乏系统研究。作者提出一种思维链分析方法来量化模型对输出定位信息的使用程度，并对 grounded reasoning 训练方案进行详细消融，同时构建合成任务与需要不可描述视觉指代的 BrickVision 基准。结果显示 grounded reasoning 仅提升计数能力，在广泛空间推理与感知基准上无显著增益，其真正价值在于任务需要难以用语言描述的视觉指代时，而现有基准多可仅凭可描述文本指代解决。
papers.summary_en: Grounded reasoning, which outputs text coordinates of relevant locations within chain-of-thought, is widely used for complex visual reasoning but its benefits and limits are understudied. The authors introduce a chain-of-thought analysis method to measure how much a model uses its outputted grounding, perform a detailed ablation of a grounded reasoning training recipe, and build synthetic tasks plus BrickVision, a benchmark requiring undescribable visual references. They find grounded reasoning improves counting but yields no significant gain over non-grounded baselines across many spatial reasoning and perception benchmarks, and is most useful when tasks require undescribable references—a gap existing benchmarks largely fail to capture.
highlights_zh: 量化模型对输出定位信息的使用程度
仅计数提升，广泛基准无显著增益
揭示不可描述指代的关键作用与基准缺口

papers.title: OopsieRecover: Learning Transferable VLA Corrections from Semantic Interventions
papers.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models can perform a wide range of robotic manipulation tasks, but often fail during deployment. Teaching them to recover from these failures requires substantial corrective data: existing approaches learn to recover from failures by directly associating corrective actions with the observations in which they were demonstrated. For instance, DAgger-like fine-tuning can require tens to hundreds of interactions, yet the resulting policy may still fail to generalize the learned corrections beyond the demonstrated scenarios. We hypothesize that semantics can capture the underlying reasons for failures and their corrections, enabling policies to learn from only a handful of corrective demonstrations and generalize those corrections to novel objects, and scene variations. We propose OopsieRecover, a framework that uses abduction to infer the intent behind a small set of corrective demonstrations and encodes the inferred knowledge as dense spatial representations and conditional costs. These costs capture when a behavior is undesirable and steer the policy toward more desirable action regions. We experiment across 6 tasks and variations in object poses, scenes, and related tasks, and find that only a handful of corrective demonstrations can enable a VLA to overcome failures across a broad range of novel situations, without requiring new corrective data for each variation. Please refer to https://robin-lab.cs.utexas.edu/oopsierecover for videos.
papers.summary_zh: VLA模型在机器人操作部署中常失败，而现有恢复方法需大量纠正数据且难以泛化。OopsieRecover通过溯因推理从小样本纠正演示中推断意图，并将其编码为密集空间表示和条件代价以引导策略。在6个任务及多种变化上，仅需少量演示即可让VLA克服新场景中的失败，无需为每种变化采集新数据。
papers.summary_en: VLA models often fail during robotic manipulation deployment, and existing recovery methods require substantial corrective data while generalizing poorly. OopsieRecover uses abduction to infer intent from a handful of corrective demonstrations and encodes it as dense spatial representations and conditional costs that steer the policy. Across 6 tasks and variations, a few demonstrations enable the VLA to overcome failures in novel situations without new corrective data per variation.
highlights_zh: 溯因推断意图编码为空间代价
少量演示跨新场景泛化恢复
减少纠正数据采集成本

papers.title: Latent RL Priors for Data-Efficient Dexterous Manipulation
papers.abstract: Learning dexterous manipulation from limited visual demonstrations is challenging because policies must acquire both perceptual grounding and precise control, while reinforcement learning (RL) in simulation can acquire rich control behaviors from large-scale interaction with privileged information. We introduce \textbf{Latent RL Prior}, a two-stage framework that reuses this control knowledge for data-efficient visual policy learning. During privileged pretraining, we distill large-scale RL rollouts into a flow-matching action decoder conditioned on proprioception and latent task context. During visual adaptation, we freeze the decoder and learn a visual interface that maps images to its latent context using action supervision alone, without privileged labels or latent targets. The same decoder can further be shared across arms by learning coordinated visual contexts for bimanual manipulation. Across three simulated tasks, our method outperforms full-parameter fine-tuning of $π_{0.5}$ and GR00T N1.7 in the low-data regime; on door lifting and bimanual assembly, it surpasses full-data baselines using $10\times$ and $5\times$ fewer demonstrations, respectively. Further analysis shows that direct visual-to-latent conditioning improves adaptation performance and training stability over routing visual predictions through the pretrained state encoder. Robustness to unseen mass variation and greater linear accessibility of contact-force information in decoder representations further provide evidence of retained RL-acquired control knowledge. Project website: https://yixiaowang7.github.io/latent-rl-prior-page/.
papers.summary_zh: 从有限视觉示范中学习灵巧操作十分困难，因为策略需同时获得感知基础与精确控制，而仿真RL虽能利用特权信息习得丰富控制行为却难以直接迁移。作者提出Latent RL Prior两阶段框架：先用流匹配动作解码器将大规模RL轨迹蒸馏为以本体感觉和潜在任务上下文为条件的先验，再冻结解码器、仅用动作监督学习将图像映射到该潜在上下文的视觉接口，并可共享解码器实现双臂协调。在三个仿真任务上，该方法低数据下优于π0.5与GR00T N1.7全参数微调，门体提升与双臂装配分别用少10倍和5倍示范超越全数据基线，且对未见质量变化更鲁棒，表明RL控制知识得以保留。
papers.summary_en: Learning dexterous manipulation from limited visual demonstrations is hard because policies must acquire both perceptual grounding and precise control, while simulation RL can learn rich control behaviors from large-scale interaction with privileged information. We introduce Latent RL Prior, a two-stage framework that distills large-scale RL rollouts into a flow-matching action decoder conditioned on proprioception and latent task context, then freezes the decoder and learns a visual interface mapping images to that latent context using action supervision alone, with the same decoder shareable across arms for bimanual manipulation. Across three simulated tasks it outperforms full-parameter fine-tuning of π0.5 and GR00T N1.7 in the low-data regime, surpasses full-data baselines on door lifting and bimanual assembly with 10× and 5× fewer demonstrations, and shows robustness to unseen mass variation, evidencing retained RL-acquired control knowledge.
highlights_zh: 冻结RL蒸馏解码器，仅学视觉到潜在上下文映射
少10倍示范超越全数据基线（门体提升）
依赖仿真特权预训练，真实场景迁移待验证

papers.title: XStack: A Benchmark for ML Repo Migration
papers.abstract: ML code should run where researchers choose, not where it was first written. Today, machine learning code mainly lives in two ecosystems, PyTorch on NVIDIA GPUs and JAX on Google TPUs. Migrating repositories between them means building and testing across frameworks and hardware. This migration is (1) a practical need, since it unlocks different hardware for researchers, and (2) a natural benchmark: it involves different frameworks and hardware, covers whole repositories, and is long-horizon and challenging. We introduce XStack, a benchmark that evaluates agents on migrating ML repositories between these two ecosystems. Each agent receives a PyTorch repository and a clean TPU machine and must deliver a JAX repository. Its output passes if it meets our grading criteria, based on the source repository's published result, authenticated and calibrated by us. Migration by agents remains unreliable: Claude Opus 5 passes 75%, GPT-5.6-sol 45%, and every other agent at most 40%. XStack is a step toward freeing ML code from its ecosystem. We release XStack to make progress toward reliable migration across frameworks and hardware measurable.
papers.summary_zh: ML代码目前主要绑定在PyTorch+NVIDIA GPU和JAX+Google TPU两大生态中，跨框架、跨硬件的仓库迁移既有实际需求又具挑战性。作者提出XStack基准，让智能体接收PyTorch仓库并在干净的TPU机器上交付可运行的JAX仓库，以源仓库已发表结果为依据进行认证和校准评分。结果显示迁移仍不可靠：Claude Opus 5通过率75%、GPT-5.6-sol 45%、其余智能体均不超过40%，该基准为可度量的可靠跨生态迁移迈出一步。
papers.summary_en: ML code is largely locked into two ecosystems, PyTorch on NVIDIA GPUs and JAX on Google TPUs, making cross-framework and cross-hardware repository migration both a practical need and a challenging long-horizon benchmark. The authors introduce XStack, a benchmark in which an agent receives a PyTorch repository and a clean TPU machine and must deliver a JAX repository, graded against the source repository's published results that they authenticate and calibrate. Migration remains unreliable—Claude Opus 5 passes 75%, GPT-5.6-sol 45%, and all other agents at most 40%—making XStack a measurable step toward freeing ML code from its ecosystem.
highlights_zh: 跨框架跨硬件整仓库迁移基准
最高通过率75%（Claude Opus 5）
解锁异构硬件，迁移仍不可靠
